transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, like I can’t shut the motor off. Lately it’s been starting to get me in trouble at the firehouse, and I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Would you say this revved-up feeling is something you experience pretty much all the time, or does it come and go in distinct stretches, like lasting several days at a time?

It’s pretty much all the time. It doesn’t feel like it comes in stretches for a few days and then goes away. It’s more like I’m always running hot, like I can’t really shut the motor off. And lately that constant feeling has been causing problems for me at the firehouse.
Thinking back, would you say you've felt this kind of restless, motor-always-running feeling since you were a kid, or is this something that really started later, as an adult?

Yeah, since I was a kid. My mom says I was like this back in grade school too—couldn’t stay in my seat, would blurt out answers, lose homework, that kind of thing. I’d get notes sent home even though I was smart enough to do the work.
Have you noticed any physical changes recently, like unexplained weight loss, feeling unusually hot or sweaty, a racing heart, or shakiness in your hands?

No, not that I’ve noticed. My weight’s been about the same, and I haven’t had anything like shaky hands or feeling hot out of nowhere. I mean, I get sweaty and my heart gets going on calls, but that seems like the job, not something random.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like health, work, or family—and having trouble controlling that worry?
I don’t know that I’d call it excessive worry. I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, family, money sometimes—but it doesn’t feel like I’m stuck worrying all day and can’t control it.
